questionText: Complete the zero conditional: 'If you ______ water, it ______.'
explanation: Le 'zero conditional' (if + présent, présent) est utilisé pour des vérités générales ou des faits scientifiques. 'If you heat water, it boils' est une vérité universelle.

questionText: Complete the first conditional: 'If it ______ tomorrow, I ______ stay at home.'
explanation: Le 'first conditional' (if + présent, will + base verb) est utilisé pour des situations réelles ou probables dans le futur. 'If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home.'

questionText: Complete the second conditional: 'If I ______ a million CFA, I ______ travel the world.'
explanation: Le 'second conditional' (if + past simple, would + base verb) est utilisé pour des situations hypothétiques ou imaginaires dans le présent/futur. 'If I had a million CFA, I would travel the world.'

questionText: Complete the third conditional: 'If she ______ harder, she ______ the exam.'
explanation: Le 'third conditional' (if + past perfect, would have + past participle) est utilisé pour des situations hypothétiques dans le passé. 'If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.'

questionText: Complete the zero conditional: 'If the temperature ______ below zero, water ______.'
explanation: Le 'zero conditional' (if + présent, présent) est utilisé pour les faits scientifiques. 'If the temperature falls below zero, water freezes.'

questionText: Complete the first conditional: 'We ______ late if we ______ now.'
explanation: Le 'first conditional' (if + présent, will + base verb) est utilisé pour une situation future probable. 'We will be late if we don't leave now.'

questionText: Complete the second conditional: 'If I ______ you, I ______ accept that job.'
explanation: Dans le 'second conditional', on utilise souvent 'were' à toutes les personnes pour donner un conseil. 'If I were you, I would accept that job.'

questionText: Complete the third conditional: 'They ______ the game if the referee ______ that penalty.'
explanation: Le 'third conditional' (if + past perfect, would have + past participle) exprime un regret sur le passé. 'They would have won the game if the referee hadn't given that penalty.'

questionText: Which sentence is a mixed conditional?
options: If I study hard, I will pass.
If I had studied, I would have passed.
If I had studied, I would be a doctor now.
If I studied, I would pass.
explanation: Le 'mixed conditional' combine une condition au passé avec un résultat présent. 'If I had studied, I would be a doctor now.' (Si j'avais étudié, je serais médecin maintenant.)

questionText: Complete the mixed conditional: 'If she ______ (not / be) so shy, she ______ (get) the job already.'
explanation: Ce 'mixed conditional' (if + past simple, would have + past participle) exprime une condition présente (elle est timide) avec un résultat passé (elle n'a pas eu le job).

questionText: Complete the second conditional to express a wish: 'I wish I ______ more time to spend with my family.'
explanation: Après 'I wish', on utilise le passé simple (comme dans le second conditional) pour exprimer un souhait ou un regret sur le présent. 'I wish I had more time to spend with my family.'

questionText: Complete the third conditional to express a regret: 'I ______ (not / make) that mistake if you ______ (warn) me.'
explanation: Le 'third conditional' (if + past perfect, would have + past participle) exprime un regret sur le passé. 'I wouldn't have made that mistake if you had warned me.'

questionText: Identify the mixed conditional: 'If I ______ (not / eat) so much, I ______ (not / feel) sick now.'
explanation: Ce 'mixed conditional' (if + past perfect, would + base verb) exprime une condition passée avec un résultat présent. 'If I hadn't eaten so much, I wouldn't feel sick now.'

questionText: Complete the second conditional: 'If I ______ (can) fly, I ______ (visit) every country.'
explanation: Le 'second conditional' exprime une situation imaginaire. 'If I could fly, I would visit every country.'

questionText: Complete the zero conditional: 'If you ______ (mix) red and blue, you ______ (get) purple.'
explanation: Le 'zero conditional' (if + présent, présent) est utilisé pour des faits scientifiques ou des vérités générales. 'If you mix red and blue, you get purple.'

questionText: Complete the first conditional: 'She ______ (call) you if she ______ (have) time.'
explanation: Le 'first conditional' (if + présent, will + base verb) est utilisé pour une situation future probable. 'She will call you if she has time.'

questionText: Complete the mixed conditional: 'If I ______ (not / stay) up late last night, I ______ (not / feel) tired this morning.'
explanation: Ce 'mixed conditional' (if + past perfect, would + base verb) exprime une condition passée avec un résultat présent. 'If I hadn't stayed up late last night, I wouldn't feel tired this morning.'

questionText: Complete the third conditional: 'If we ______ (know) about the traffic, we ______ (take) another route.'
explanation: Le 'third conditional' (if + past perfect, would have + past participle) est utilisé pour des regrets sur le passé. 'If we had known about the traffic, we would have taken another route.'

questionText: Complete the second conditional to express a wish: 'I wish I ______ (speak) English fluently.'
explanation: Après 'I wish', on utilise le passé simple (comme dans le second conditional) pour exprimer un souhait sur le présent. 'I wish I spoke English fluently.'

questionText: Complete the mixed conditional: 'If I ______ (not / spend) all my money yesterday, I ______ (be) able to buy a new phone today.'
explanation: Ce 'mixed conditional' (if + past perfect, would + base verb) exprime une condition passée avec un résultat présent. 'If I hadn't spent all my money yesterday, I would be able to buy a new phone today.'
